description: Armande Aboudrar-Méda and Giacomo Falchetta publish URBADAPT-HEAT for city-scale heat risk and adaptation planning. Zenodo archives the public release under CC0 1.0 and links a Python repository. The description names 40 European city configurations, roughly 100 m heat hazard layers, a 2020 baseline and projections to 2050 under four climate scenarios. Modules combine age-stratified exposure, mortality functions, social vulnerability and adaptation choices such as air conditioning, street trees and early warning. The pipeline can compare public and private cost-benefit outcomes and portfolio trade-offs. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this heat-specific platform. Coverage is configured cities and chosen climate inputs, not measured future mortality. A limitation is that large inputs are fetched separately from Google Drive manifests and public APIs; source access and licences need checking per city. Calibration choices and interactions between interventions affect results. The code and inputs were not downloaded or run, and benefits were not reproduced.
